fix_commit.message: Bug 1987290 - Part 1: Use get() instead of operator[] to get arguments in FinalizationRegistryObject::unregister. r=jonco
fix_commit.author: Rong "Mantle" Bao

findings.title: Out-of-bounds argument read in FinalizationRegistryObject::unregister when called with no arguments
findings.message: As part of adding symbol-target support for FinalizationRegistry (Bug 1863140 Part 3), the code in FinalizationRegistryObject::unregister was refactored to accept non-object unregister tokens (via CanBeHeldWeakly) by first fetching the raw argument with `args[0]` into a RootedValue, and only afterwards validating it with CanBeHeldWeakly(). Previously the code validated `args.get(0).isObject()` (a bounds-safe accessor that returns UndefinedValue when the argument is missing) before ever indexing into args. By moving the unchecked `args[0]` access ahead of the validation, calling `FinalizationRegistry.prototype.unregister()` with zero arguments causes CallArgs::operator[] to be invoked with index 0 while argc_ is 0, tripping the `MOZ_ASSERT(i < argc_)` bounds assertion in js/public/CallArgs.h (and in non-debug/release builds, an out-of-bounds read of the arguments vector). The fix (Bug 1987290) replaces `args[0]` with the bounds-safe `args.get(0)`, which returns JS::UndefinedValue when argc is insufficient instead of indexing out of bounds.
findings.suggestion: Use the bounds-safe CallArgs::get() accessor instead of operator[] when the argument is optional / argc is not yet validated. get(0) returns UndefinedValue() when argc is 0 (or less than the requested index), avoiding any out-of-bounds access, and CanBeHeldWeakly(UndefinedValue) correctly evaluates to false so the existing TypeError path is still taken when no token is supplied.

ground_truth.root_cause: Bug 1863140 Part 3 (commit 321172222a2e) refactored FinalizationRegistry.register/unregister to support non-object (e.g. symbol) targets/unregister tokens via a new CanBeHeldWeakly() helper. While doing so, the unregister() function's existing safe pattern of `args.get(0).isObject()` followed by `&args[0].toObject()` (indexing only after confirming the argument existed and was an object) was replaced by directly constructing `RootedValue unregisterToken(cx, args[0])` ahead of any validation, re-introducing an unchecked array index into the native call arguments before verifying argc covers that index.
